newsitem.title: USA: Sequa says jury finds in unit's favor.
newsitem.headline: Sequa says jury finds in unit's favor.

text.p: Sequa Corp said on Tuesday that a Texas jury found that United Technologies Corp's Pratt & Whitney division "had willfully and flagrantly violated the Texas Free Enterprise and Antitrust Act of 1983."

In a unanimous decision in favor of the Chromalloy Gas Turbine Corp, a unit of Sequa, the jury found that Pratt illegally attempted to monopolize the replacement business for Pratt & Whitney jet engine parts, Sequa said.
United Technologies spokesmen were not immediately available.

Sequa said that based on the jury's specific finding that Pratt's attempt to monopolize was "willful" and "flagrant," Chromalloy is entitled to injunctive relief to prohibit such illegal conduct. The jury, which sat in Bexar County court, declined to award monetary relief.

"The jury's decision offers major financial benefits to the airlines -- and ultimately to all of us who buy airline tickets -- because it means that airlines will continue to have cost-effective maintenance and repair options available," said Martin Weinstein, chairman of Chromalloy.
"Chromalloy and other independent repair vendors provide high-quality component repairs at up to five times less than the cost of buying new spare parts from the engine maker," he said.
